description: VN 'tôi có/được N tuổi' transfer: learners calque to 'I have N years old' where English age uses BE ('I am N years old'). Rule en-vietlish-age-have-be replaces have/has with the agreeing BE form (I->am, you/we/they->are, he/she/it->is) ONLY in a pronoun-subject + have/has + 1-3 digit number + year(s) old frame, and normalizes the predicate to 'years old'.
fp_risk_note: Low risk. The trailing 'old' predicate is mandatory, so possessive-compound ('a 20-year-old son'), partitive ('20 years of experience'), and plain possession ('20 books') never match. Already-correct 'I am 20 years old' is untouched because the frame requires have/has. Subject scope is the closed pronoun list, so noun subjects are out of scope.

positive.notes: 'I have N years old' -> 'I am N years old'.
3rd-singular 'She has N years old' -> 'She is N years old'.
Plural 'We have N years old' -> 'We are N years old'.
Singular 'year' captured and normalized to 'years old' (engine real output).

negative.notes: Already correct (BE present) -> frame requires have/has, must abstain.
Possessive-compound '20-year-old son'; no 'years old' predicate -> must abstain.
Partitive 'years of', not 'years old' -> must abstain.
Plain possession, no age predicate -> must abstain.
